newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ATHLETICS: GAINSFORD-TAYLOR COMES IN FOURTH
Australian sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Taylor has been beaten into fourth place in the 200 metres event at the Nice Grand Prix athletics meeting.
Jamaica's Merlene Ottey returned to winning form to run down Gainsford-Taylor who led by almost a metre after turning into the straight.
Fellow Australian Margaret Crowley finished strongly to finish third in the women's mile.
HUNTER DISPUTE: UNION WANTS COLLECTIVE AGREEMENT
A new stance put forward by the miners' union in the bitter Hunter Valley coal dispute has been followed by a letter to Rio Tinto calling for a re-opening of negotiations.
The CFMEU believes it is possible to negotiate while its members remain on strike.
Union president John Maitland has written to mine manager Allan Davies saying the union accepts the decision of seven Hunter Valley Number One mine workers to accept individual contracts.
Mr Maitland has asked Rio Tinto to accept the balance of miners, over 400 workers, seeks a collection agreement.
The union wants to begin talks on a collective agreement while miners remain on strike, an option Mr Davies said he will consider.
He said the union has made a positive move and he will consider re-entering negotiations with the CFMEU over the next few days.
Mr Maitland has also asked Rio Tinto not to again attempt to transport coal from the mine.
He said to do so would not be in Australia's best interests, because it may risk an escalation of the dispute, which he said the union is trying to contain to the Hunter region.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister John Howard says the Miners Union is exporting Australian jobs by writing to customers of Rio Tinto, warning them the dispute at the Hunter Valley Number One Mine is likely to be protracted.
Mr Howard has also denied claims by ACTU President Jennie George that he wants a national industrial dispute based on the dispute at the mine.
HOWARD EMBRACES UNLIKELY BEDFELLOW
The Labor Party and the ACTU should take note of comments by former Prime Minister Bob Hawke and respect the Coalition's industrial mandate, Prime Minister John Howard said yesterday.

On ABC Radio yesterday, Mr Hawke said while he may disagree with its policies, the Coalition was elected with a large majority and the trade union movement and the ALP owe it to Australia to stop obstructing the Coalition's industrial agenda.
Mr Howard told more than 400 people at a Liberal Party function in Newcastle last night Mr Hawke's comments give weight to the Coalition's stance in the Rio Tinto dispute in the Hunter Valley.
He said the ACTU and the ALP should take note of the advice from the Labor Party's most successful leader this century.

"I think he speaks commonsense. We did get a thumping majority, the Labor Party and the unions may not like our industrial relations policy, but they should in the national interest, take Mr Hawke's advice," Mr Howard said.
BLACK PANTHER STILL BATTLING TO STAY
Lawyers for American activist Lorenzo Ervin have confirmed they have been given a short extension to answer Immigration Department questions.
Mr Ervin, a former Black Panther, yesterday said he is being denied natural justice by the short deadlines being imposed by the Department.

Mr Ervin's Brisbane-based legal team said they received on Monday an Immigration Department request for answers to 36 questions relating to his character, in order for his Australian visa to remain current.
Mr Ervin's lawyers said they were originally given until yesterday afternoon to answer the questions, but now have until 4pm today to comply.
However Mr Ervin's lawyers doubt they will be able to accumulate all the requested documentation in that time.
Mr Ervin said most of the questions relate to his political affiliation and activism, but he was unable to provide the
information within the original time limit.
TODDLER'S BABYSITTER CHARGED WITH MURDER
The babysitter of missing Victorian toddler, Jaidyn Leskie, will re-appear in the Melbourne Magistrate's Court today charged with the murder of the 14-month-old from Moe, east of Melbourne.
Greg Domaszewicz, 28, told an out of sessions hearing at the Melbourne Custody Centre, he is accused of something he has not done.
Police asked for bail to be refused, and when asked if there was a reason why he should be given bail, Mr Domaszewicz replied: "I'm not guilty of anything.".
Mr Domaszewicz, the boyfriend of Jaidyn's mother, Bylinda Murphy, was minding the toddler at his Newborough house in Moe before reporting him missing more than four weeks ago.
Despite a huge air, water and land search including the Moe tip, homicide detectives have been unable to find the boy.
Mr Domaszewicz was questioned by police for five hours yesterday after his car was intercepted in the Melbourne metropolitan area.
HOWARD UPBEAT ABOUT JOB PROSPECTS
The Prime Minister, John Howard, has given an upbeat prediction on the prospects for employment growth during his visit to Newcastle.
He says he can't recall a period during the last 20 or 30 years when there has been such a fortunate conjunction of economic figures.
The Prime Minister has nominated low inflation, falling interest rates, expanding growth, strong business investment, falling budget deficits and a positive international economic climate.
Mr Howard says there is a strong base for jobs growth.
"Now you take those five or six things together and you have an underpinning and a base for employment growth the like of which we haven't seen for the last 20 years," he said.
"Now that's the good news, that's the positive news and that's the optimistic side of it."
AFL: CARLTON'S MADDEN RETIRES
Football fans have seen the last of Carlton ruckman, Justin Madden on the field.
Madden has officially ended his 332 game career, citing injury as the main reason for his immediate retirement.
The 36-year old says he also doesn't have the drive to continue.
"I suppose one of the other things about league football is to get a kick, you've got to be an angry young man with a chip on your shoulder," Madden said.
"And I haven't been an angry young man for some time, and I'm probably a bit tired of pretending I'm an angry young man with a chip on my shoulder."
Carlton and Essendon have decided to play for the "Madden Trophy", in honour of Justin and his brother, former Essendon ruckman, Simon, who have togther played more than 700 senior matches.
Justin will do a lap of honour before the Carlton, Essendon game at the MCG on Saturday.
